title: Quad layout quantization stalls in branch-and-bound on crawfish IMG_4113
description: On crawfish IMG_4113 (and on IMG_4116 with CRAW-143's cone separation) quad_layout's arc quantization runs branch-and-bound for minutes with the incumbent fixed and the bound barely moving, e.g. `nodes=204752 open=85039 incumbent=35492.145 bound=35481.120 220s` (CRAW-146 worktree log). Runs only end at the scene timeout. Find why this instance is hard (which constraints keep the relaxation loose, how many variables, whether a few near-tied classes cause it) the way LCK21a's quantization intends, fix it so it solves in seconds like the other scans (0.1-3.8 s), and make a stall fail with a clear message within a measured budget instead of spinning.
definition-of-done:
1. The cause of the stall on IMG_4113 is shown with numbers (variables, constraints, gap over time, what keeps the bound from rising) saved under tmp/.
2. A fix following LCK21a makes IMG_4113's quantization finish in seconds, with the furthest quad_layout stage reported before and after.
3. A quantization that cannot close its gap fails within a budget with a message naming the gap, instead of running until an outer timeout.
4. The 11 suite models and the T-Rex skull give the same quantization objective and quad counts; ixd wt perf shows no regression.
testing-plan:
1. Reproduce on IMG_4113 (with CRAW-146's repair if it has not landed) and record the gap over time.
2. A unit test with a small integer program that stalls the old way and finishes or fails cleanly after.
3. Suite models, skull, ixd wt perf.
